opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kenneth Burch (employee ID E007) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E007.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kenneth Burch (E007) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, the maximum is write (admin would require the Payroll Specialist role, which the Analyst role does not own). Requested level is at the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows Kenneth Burch (E007) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, maximum is read. Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: There is a conflict in the records: the HR note lists Kenneth Burch as a full-time Analyst (max write), while the Security note lists him as a contractor with basic security training (max read, since write requires advanced training). Given the conflicting employment-type evidence, the conservative decision is to grant the level that is within policy under both interpretations. Since read is allowed for both full-time employees and contractors with basic training, and the request for write cannot be confirmed as permissible, I grant read.
